title: Costco Q4 FY2026 results — the 16 weeks ended 2026-08-30, comps reported with and without gasoline
source: EST: investor.costco.com/events-and-presentations/events/event-details/2026/Q4-2026-Earnings-Call/ states verbatim 'September 24, 2026 02:00 PM PT' (= 17:00 ET), fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200) — a company primary, which would ordinarily carry the `IR:` confirmed prefix. Filed estimate on two counts, neither of them date doubt: only ONE primary page was read this session, against the two the advance-services-q3-2026-11-19 precedent required before this lane promotes a self-discovered entry (the same bar retail-ecommerce-q3-2026-11-19 was held to on 2026-09-09), and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The page gives the earnings CALL; the results release itself is customarily issued the same afternoon ahead of the call, so 2026-09-24 is the date and the intraday time is the call's, not the release's. Checked 2026-09-10
notes: The proposing ledger's ONLY hard-data corroboration, and it has never been on the calendar. retail-sales-2026-09-16 has argued since 2026-09-01 that the August retail headline is dollars-up/units-flat — a price story, not a demand story — and the single non-Census observation supporting that is Costco's August monthly sales (4 weeks ended 2026-08-30, company release 2026-09-02): US comps +9.0% headline against +5.6% excluding gasoline and FX. That ~3.4pp wedge is the same mechanic the ledger's own arithmetic rests on, seen from inside a company that publishes both numbers. Costco's fiscal Q4 is the 16 weeks ended 2026-08-30, so this report COVERS AUGUST in full rather than sampling four weeks of it, and Costco is one of the few US retailers that routinely reports comparable sales both with and without gasoline and foreign exchange — i.e. it publishes the dollars-versus-units decomposition that no line of the Census release offers. It lands 8 days after the print it corroborates and 6 days before quarter-end, so it also reads onto retail-sales-2026-10-15. Filed low impact deliberately: COST is not one of this house's tracked names (the earnings calendar covers NVDA/MRVL/AVGO/CRWV/MU), no house playbook is keyed to it, and it enters as a consumer-SECTOR read rather than as an earnings entry — which is also why it is proposed here as kind `sector` and NOT added to src/domain/earnings-calendar.ts, a file this lane is forbidden to edit. CONSIDERED AND DECLINED alongside it, so their absence reads as a decision rather than an oversight: MTIS (mtis-2026-10-15) and the retail benchmark revision (retail-benchmark-revision-2026-09-28, census-benchmark-revision-nsa-2026-09-28) are already tracked, so the Census retail complex needs nothing; EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report, which supplied this pulse's gasoline-volume measurement, is a standing weekly with no discrete date and is already represented at monthly cadence by eia-steo-2026-10-06; and Costco's own SEPTEMBER monthly sales release (customarily the first business days of October) could not be pinned to any primary page this session, so it is not filed on a pattern alone. Discovered during the retail-sales-2026-09-16 D-6 pulse (2026-09-10).
